briefings.headline: Be selective against Eovaldi; make the fastball count
briefings.message: Nathan Eovaldi is the high-confidence (85%) predicted starter. He leans on the splitter, so make him prove he can land it for a strike; hunt fastballs and don’t chase offspeed. Yordan Alvarez leads off with the clearest matchup edge—look to drive fastballs. Respect Eovaldi’s curveball below the zone. If he exits, watch left-hander Jacob Latz and right-hander Jakob Junis in the Texas bullpen.
reminders: Alvarez: hunt fastballs; avoid chasing the splitter.
Taylor Trammell’s fastball results are promising, but his samples are small.
Stay patient with two strikes and don’t expand against breaking balls.

briefings.message: Spencer Arrighetti starts; plan for 5.0 innings with a 90-pitch limit. Lead with curveballs and sweepers, and locate fastballs carefully—especially against left-handed bats. Use Steven Okert for a key left-handed matchup; Bryan King and Enyel De Los Santos are limited, so save them for necessity.
reminders: Keep Arrighetti’s fastballs out of the middle.
